item.description:
Grab some dinner and a pint while enjoying our long-running Old-Time Jam! Featuring many talented musicians from the local WNC area, our traditional Appalachian mountain music jam runs from 5-9pm every Wednesday night at Jack of the Wood! Jack Of The Wood is still a downtown hot spot for food, brews and drink since 1997 and founders Joan and Joe Eckert who still own it, have maintained the original lively English and Irish vibe. The old-time mountain and Irish music jams continue, including a hot bluegrass jam Thursdays and brunch every Sunday. The venue extends a welcoming feeling to regulars and newcomers to this day. https://jackofthewood.com/

item.title: Jam > Grass > Jam: The Saylor Brothers — Wed Sep 16, 6:30 PM — French Broad River Brewery
item.description:
The Saylor Brothers are a jamgrass fusion group from Asheville, fronted by brothers Will & Ben Saylor, of Brushfire Stankgrass. This project is a foray further into the realm of bluegrass jam, with more emphasis on improvisation piled on top of a structure of traditional bluegrass and innovative original songwriting. As a trio with Greg Stiglets on bass, the band packs a large sound coming from three acoustic instruments, and often adds a fourth player for further improvisational and bluegrass firepower.
Jam > Grass > Jam is not an open bluegrass jam but is a residency featuring a rotating casts of special guests from Asheville’s bluegrass/jamband scene.
French Broad River Brewery is more than just a place to enjoy a drink—it’s a community hub where great beer, delicious pizza, live music, and good times come together. item.title: Saman Majeed, Ph. D. — Forensic Science & Law — Thu Sep 17, 12:00 AM
item.description:

Head to the Mullen & James Humanities Hall to learn more about how forensic science can inform investigations, evidence, and the pursuit of justice. This event is presented by the Department of Interdisciplinary Studies and UNC Asheville’s Law, Ethics, and Social Policy program. This is the first of three events in the Fall 2026 Interdisciplinary Studies Guest Speaker Series. Additional events include a discussion from Guest Speaker David Firestein on September 30 and a presentation from Professor Austin Hooe, Ph. D. on November 5.

item.title: How to Overcome Anger — Sun Sep 20, 10:30 AM
item.description:
Meditation in Asheville: Meditation and Modern Buddhism How to Overcome Anger with Modern Buddhism Teacher Kadam Sharon Lovich
Anger appears in many forms and disguises. Sometimes it manifests as a feeling of stress, other times it may take the form of depression. From the slightest frustration to resentment and embittered rage, anger is an emotion we all need to understand and conquer if we are to enjoy and make the most out of our life. In this series we will explore practical solutions to the problem of anger, deconstructing its actual causes and learning viable alternatives to this painful habit of mind. Cost: $12 (free and online options for members) [Read More and Register](https://www.meditationinasheville.org/sunday-drop-in-meditation-class/) [Become a Member](https://www.meditationinasheville.org/become-a-member/)

item.title: Cataloochee Valley ELK (GSMNP) — Tue Sep 22, 11:30 AM
item.description: Hendo Fun Friends I am going to Cataloochee Valley in the Smoky Mtn Nat'l Pk to explore, picnic and, hopefully, **catch the Elk during their 'rut' bugling.** Up to 16 are welcome to join me. This event is suitable for non-hikers and “grade school-age” grandchildren. **Since the storm destroyed much of the valley road, we will park near the church and see how far we can walk into the valley.** The elk usually overnight in the valley. Usually, by 4-5pm. There is never a guarantee. But, if we get lucky, it's an event not to be missed. Cataloochee Valley has a historical home, church and barn which we will take time to explore. **The plan is to arrive early afternoon to give time to explore and 'PICNIC' before the elk 'present' themselves.** Bring a folding chair, bug spray, camera, water & food. Hiking NOT required. **We are the Sloth Hike Team of WNC: “We will get there when we get there.” We dare to go where the ‘real’ hike groups don’t !!** **https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Bsh_8qxUfDY

item.title: Asheville Crokinole Club — Tue Sep 22, 6:00 PM — Taproom At Highland Brewing Co.
item.description:
Crokinole Tuesdays at Highland Brewing Taproom Join us every Tuesday in the Taproom for an evening of flicks, strategy, and friendly competition! We’re hosting the Asheville Crokinole Club—a community of players who love this classic dexterity board game. Never played? No problem! Crokinole is easy to learn and endlessly fun. Players take turns flicking wooden discs across a circular board, aiming for the high-scoring center zones. The twist? If your opponent has discs on the board, you must hit one—miss, and your piece is out! Whether you’re a seasoned pro or just curious, come grab a pint, meet new friends, and test your skills.
Source: Highland Brewing

item.description:
Meditation in Asheville: Meditation and Modern Buddhism All In: The Power of Determinations with Modern Buddhism Teacher Kadam Sharon Lovich
Whether it’s everyday stress, sadness, or even anger, our suffering can be transformed into inner strength, love, and joy. The first step is understanding its source. In this series, we’ll explore Buddha’s teachings on the Four Noble Truths. The Four Noble Truths are the essence of Buddhist thought and gives us a clear, precise way to understand our life and how to move forward in it. Through teachings and meditation, we’ll discover that suffering comes not from external conditions, but from our own mind. Recognizing this opens the door to transforming our experience and uncovering a more lasting, genuine happiness. item.title: Partnering for our future: Warren Wilson’s Applied Climate Studies Program makes recovery and resilience the center of learning — Mon Sep 28, 6:00 PM
item.description:
Two years after Helene, graduate students in Warren Wilson’s MS in Applied Climate Studies (MACS) program will present on the process and outcomes of their engaged research projects. These projects sit at the center of the MACS program, which prioritizes learning through both cooperation and application. From their first week, MACS students are guided in linking their classroom material with impactful projects. Students spend two years working collaboratively with peers and alongside established community partners throughout their degree, leaving the program with concrete experience and skills in addressing present and pressing climate change challenges. Insights about building more resilient communities and ecosystems will be shared.
Source: Warren Wilson College

item.title: How to Overcome Anger — Sun Oct 4, 10:30 AM
item.description:
Meditation in Asheville: Meditation and Modern Buddhism How to Overcome Anger with Modern Buddhism Teacher Kadam Sharon Lovich
Anger appears in many forms and disguises. Sometimes it manifests as a feeling of stress, other times it may take the form of depression. From the slightest frustration to resentment and embittered rage, anger is an emotion we all need to understand and conquer if we are to enjoy and make the most out of our life. In this series we will explore practical solutions to the problem of anger, deconstructing its actual causes and learning viable alternatives to this painful habit of mind. Cost: $12 (free and online options for members) [Read More and Register](https://www.meditationinasheville.org/sunday-drop-in-meditation-class/) [Become a Member](https://www.meditationinasheville.org/become-a-member/)
